Run NicheNet ligand activity analysis

Source: R/interop-nichenet.R
run_nichenet.Rd

A streamlined wrapper around nichenetr's ligand activity prediction workflow. Uses a ContextNetwork (with integrated GRN) to predict which ligands from sender cells regulate target genes in receiver cells.

run_nichenet(
  object,
  network,
  sender,
  receiver,
  geneset_oi,
  group_col = "cell_type",
  assay = "RNA",
  slot = "data",
  min_pct = 0.1,
  top_n_ligands = 20,
  lr_network = NULL,
  data_path = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object containing expression data

network

A ContextNetwork object from integrate_networks()

sender

Character, name of sender cell type(s) in metadata

receiver

Character, name of receiver cell type in metadata

geneset_oi

Character vector of genes of interest in receiver (e.g., differentially expressed genes). REQUIRED.

group_col

Column name in metadata containing cell type labels (default: "cell_type")

assay

Assay to use from Seurat object (default: "RNA")

slot

Slot to use for expression data (default: "data")

min_pct

Minimum percentage of cells expressing a gene to consider it expressed (default: 0.10)

top_n_ligands

Number of top ligands to return (default: 20)

lr_network

Optional ligand-receptor network. If NULL, uses nichenetr's default or loads from data_path.

data_path

Path to directory containing NicheNet data files (lr_network_human.rds, etc.). If NULL, uses nichenetr package data.

verbose

Logical, print progress messages (default: TRUE)

Value

A list containing:

  • ligand_activities: data.frame of ligand activity scores

  • ligand_target_links: data.frame of ligand-target regulatory potential

  • top_ligands: character vector of top-ranked ligands

  • receptor_info: data.frame of ligand-receptor pairs

  • nichenet_input: list of inputs used (for reproducibility)

Details

This function performs the standard NicheNet ligand activity analysis:

  1. Identifies genes expressed in sender and receiver cells

  2. Finds potential ligands (expressed in sender, receptor in receiver)

  3. Predicts ligand activities based on geneset_oi

  4. Extracts ligand-target regulatory potential

The key difference from standard NicheNet is that the ligand-target matrix comes from integrate_networks(), which incorporates your context-specific GRN.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Import and integrate GRN
grn <- import_grn("path/to/grn/")
network <- integrate_networks(grn, data_path = "path/to/nichenet_data/")

# Run NicheNet analysis
result <- run_nichenet(
    object = seurat_obj,
    network = network,
    sender = "Macrophage",
    receiver = "Fibroblast",
    geneset_oi = de_genes,
    group_col = "cell_type"
)

# Access results
head(result$ligand_activities)
result$top_ligands
} # }
